Subject: Renewal planning — EU primary + APAC hot-standby (questions)

Hi Ava / Marissa,

We are kicking off our renewal discussion for MedSync (current contract expires 12/31/2026). Priority ask from our infra team: EU must remain primary (data residency + audit controls) but we want an APAC hot-standby for traffic surges and regional latency.

High-level asks:
- Confirm if a hot-standby (warm capacity with automatic cross-region failover) is supported under the current SLA and what RTO/RPO we can realistically commit to.
- What is the cost delta for adding: a) APAC hot-standby pool sized for 10% of steady-state queries, b) a 20% capacity uplift (to cover Q1 spike).
- We are open to an annual term in exchange for a committed capacity discount; need numbers to share with procurement.

Can we set a short call this week to walk options? Also will need a draft SOW and pricing spreadsheet to circulate.

Thanks —
Liam
Principal Cloud Ops, MedSync

Thanks Liam — good to loop in early. High level response below and I've attached a draft SOW + a first-pass pricing export for your procurement team (see attachments).

Short answers:
- Hot-standby model: supported. Typical configuration is an APAC warm pool that keeps images and KV caches synced; cold-to-hot ramp for large scale is ~5–10 minutes for model weights+runtime spin-up; with prefix/KV warmup we can achieve effective RTO of ~90s for cached flows. RPO depends on the KV sync cadence; we recommend 60s on critical routes.
- Cost delta (ballpark): APAC warm standby sized at 10% steady-state -> ~+18% on hosted unit costs before discounts. 20% capacity uplift -> additional +14% on top of steady-state. If you commit to a 12-month term and a reserved uplift, we can apply a blended discount.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal alignment call: 30m technical + procurement (tomorrow slot available 09:00–11:00 UTC).
2) Redwood to provide: draft SOW (attached), pricing CSV with committed vs on-demand rows (attached), and a short runbook for a failover drill.
3) Offer: one-time onboarding credit to offset the APAC warm-standby setup if you sign a 12-month commit by 11/30.

I'll loop in Ben and Monica to confirm pricing options and the credit level.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sow-eu-apac-v1.pdf, pricing-breakdown-20261112.csv

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear asks and Ava for the draft materials. Quick summary and formal proposal so your procurement team has something concrete: 

Proposal summary:
- Term: 12 months (starts on 2027-01-01) with the option to renew at revised rates.
- Capacity: EU primary (current baseline) + APAC warm standby at 10% of steady-state, and a committed 20% uplift across both regions reserved for Q1.
- SLA / Failover: We commit to an RTO target of 90s for cached flows with recommended KV sync at 60s. We will include a failover drill runbook as an exhibit to the SOW and can execute a coordinated drill within the first 30 days of go-live.
- Commercials: Blended 12% discount on committed units vs on-demand. One-time onboarding credit of $8,000 applied to the first invoice for APAC onramp. Estimated impact: ~+30% gross spend vs current baseline before discounts; after discount and credit the net uplift is ~+14% year-over-year (detailed line items in attached pricing CSV).

Next steps:
1) Confirm acceptance of term & credit by 11/30 to lock pricing.
2) Procurement: please review attached pricing-breakdown-20261112.csv and the SOW (redwood-sow-eu-apac-v1.pdf).
3) Schedule: Proposed canary window for APAC standby: 2027-01-15 to 2027-01-21 (we will coordinate a failover drill during this window).

Liam / Sana — any restrictions from your compliance team on the failover drill (e.g., data sampling, audit steps) we should bake into the runbook? Happy to run a quick call to walk SOW exhibits and the pricing rows.
